title: deny_unknown_fields does not apply to AcState::Computed -- a unit variant under internal tagging silently accepts unknown keys
body:
`deny_unknown_fields` is a property of the VARIANT'S SHAPE, not of the enum, so `AcState::Computed` silently accepts canon it should refuse.

## The defect

`AcState` carries `#[serde(tag = "is", rename_all = "kebab-case", deny_unknown_fields)]`. Reading that attribute, every variant refuses an unknown key. **Five of six do. The unit variant does not, and never did.**

Under internal tagging a unit variant has no field set to check an unknown key against, so serde drops sibling keys in silence. Nothing fails to compile, nothing fails a round-trip, and no other test in the estate notices.

## Measured, post-0133 (`04cf6f18`), by deserialising each variant with one extra key

| variant     | shape   | clean doc accepted | unknown field REFUSED |
| ----------- | ------- | ------------------ | --------------------- |
| computed    | unit    | true               | **false**             |
| unsatisfied | struct  | true               | true                  |
| satisfied   | struct  | true               | true                  |
| descoped    | struct  | true               | true                  |
| withdrawn   | struct  | true               | true                  |
| fiat        | newtype | true               | true                  |

The discriminator is the SHAPE, not the enum's attribute and not the variant's meaning. `fiat` is the newtype case and refuses correctly, which was itself measured rather than assumed when it was added.

## Why the exposure is larger than one row of a table

`computed` is an ENTRY state -- it is where every test-backed criterion in the estate sits, and nobody writes it by hand into a state it later leaves. So the variant with no strictness is one of the two a hand-authored or migrated canon file is most likely to carry. A typo'd sibling key on a computed row is ingested silently and is unrecoverable afterwards, because nothing recorded that a key was dropped.

`unsatisfied` was the other one. It was closed as a SIDE EFFECT of 0133 widening it to carry a note -- not by anyone deciding to fix strictness. That is the part worth keeping: **the estate's protection here improved by accident, and would have regressed by accident just as easily.**

## How it was found

The strictness arm in `fiat_state_serde.rs` was written BEFORE the type moved, to check whether `deny_unknown_fields` survived through a newtype variant. It was written as a question about serde rather than about our code, and it was the control on that arm -- not the arm itself -- that exposed the unit-variant case. An arm written after the fact would have been a green collected to confirm a belief.

## The price of the fix, MEASURED rather than quoted

`Computed` -> `Computed {}`. Mirror types with the real enum's exact attributes, compared directly:

- serialised bytes: `{"is":"computed"}` from BOTH. Identical.
- existing canon (`{"is":"computed"}`): accepted by both.
- unknown field: shipped ACCEPTS, proposed REFUSES.
- generated JSON Schema: **identical** with `title` excluded -- the two mirror types must have different names to coexist, so comparing `title` would have been the instrument manufacturing its own finding. It reported a spurious difference until that was removed. A positive control (a third enum with a real extra field) confirms the comparison can still see a genuine difference.

**So nothing published moves: no face version bump, no canon rewrite, no consumer-visible change.** The fix is an implementation detail rather than a ruling.

## Not bundled into 0133 deliberately

0133 was a change hv ruled on. This is a separate defect that its strictness arm happened to expose, and folding an unruled change into a ruled one hides it.
